name: Escravos–Lagos Pipeline System (ELPS I)
capacity: 1.1 bcf/d (ELPS I); 2.2 bcf/d combined with ELPS II

source.name: NNPC Ltd / Global Energy Monitor Gas Infrastructure Tracker
source.table_or_page: ELPS project page; GEM 'Escravos-Lagos Pipeline System'

notes: Feeds Egbin, Olorunsogo, Omotosho, Geregu power plants and WAGP at Alagbado/Itoki. Intermediate points approximate (Warri, Ore).

name: Escravos–Lagos Pipeline System II (ELPS II loop)
notes: Oilserv-built parallel loop (Oben–Lagos section) completed 2023; final commissioning of all metering stations staged 2023–2024.

name: Ajaokuta–Kaduna–Kano Gas Pipeline (AKK)

source.name: NNPC Ltd
source.table_or_page: AKK River Niger crossing / mainline welding completion (Dec 2025)

notes: USD 2.8 bn. 72% complete Q1 2025; River Niger crossing July 2025; mainline welding completed 29 Dec 2025; facility hook-up and commissioning slated 2026 (NNPC guidance: in service mid-2026). Phase 1 of the Trans-Nigeria Gas Pipeline (TNGP).

name: Obiafu–Obrikom–Oben Gas Pipeline (OB3)

source.name: NNPC Ltd / GEM
source.table_or_page: GEM OB3 page; NNPC River Niger crossing completion (Apr 2026)

notes: USD 700 m. Links eastern gas network to ELPS and AKK. Mechanically complete except the River Niger HDD crossing, which was completed April 2026; commissioning expected 2026. Status as of end-2025: under construction (final crossing).

name: Trans-Niger Pipeline (TNP)
operator: Renaissance Africa Energy (ex-SPDC JV; NNPC 55%, Renaissance 30%, TotalEnergies 10%, AENR 5%)

source.name: Shell plc / Renaissance Africa Energy
source.table_or_page: Completion of SPDC sale to Renaissance (13 Mar 2025)

notes: Rumuekpe–Bodo–Bonny export terminal, Bonny Light. Operated by Renaissance since March 2025. Repeated sabotage/fire incidents (2025). Length approximate; two parallel lines.

name: Trans-Forcados Pipeline (TFP)
notes: Feeds Forcados Oil Terminal; alternative Trans-Escravos / Trans-Ramos routes used during outages. Approximate geometry.

name: Nembe Creek Trunk Line (NCTL)
notes: Nembe Creek to Bonny (Cawthorne Channel); frequent shut-ins for theft/vandalism 2022–2024.

name: NNPC System 2B products pipeline (Atlas Cove–Mosimi–Ibadan–Ilorin)
notes: Most NNPC refined-products lines (Systems 2A–2E) are idle since the 2010s due to vandalism; refineries restarted (Port Harcourt/Warri 2024–2025) rely on trucking. Included for completeness; status 'offline' as of 2024–2025.

name: West African Gas Pipeline (WAGP)
operator: West African Gas Pipeline Company (WAPCo): Chevron 36.9%, NNPC 25%, Shell 18%, Takoradi Power 16.3%, SoBeGaz 2%, SoToGaz 2%
capacity: 474 mmcf/d design (2024 avg ~180 mmcf/d; 2025 avg ~218 mmcf/d)

source.name: WAPCo / GEM
source.table_or_page: WAPCo official updates 2025; GEM 'West African Gas Pipeline'

notes: Alagbado/Itoki (ELPS tie-in) – Lagos Beach – Cotonou – Lomé – Tema – Takoradi. Reverse flow capability Takoradi–Tema (TTIP, 2019) lets Ghanaian domestic gas flow east. 2025 record throughput (~80 m MMBtu, 99.8% reliability).

name: Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline (TSGP / NIGAL)
notes: Warri–Ajaokuta–Kano (Nigerian section = AKK + Kano–Niger border extension) – Zinder – Agadez – Tamanrasset – In Salah – Hassi R'Mel. Est. USD 13 bn. Ministerial revival Oct 2024 / 2025; no FID. Niger political situation (2023 coup) remains a constraint.

name: Nigeria–Morocco Gas Pipeline (NMGP / African Atlantic Gas Pipeline)
notes: Est. USD 25 bn; FEED completed; Moroccan-section tenders launched 2025; first phase would cover Morocco–Mauritania–Senegal. Route mostly offshore along the Atlantic coast. Equatorial Guinea signed a 2024 MoU for a Gulf of Guinea feeder link.

name: Niger–Benin Crude Export Pipeline (Agadem–Sèmè / WAPCO pipeline)
operator: West African Oil Pipeline Company (WAPCo, CNPC)

source.name: Niger Ministry of Petroleum / CNPC; Bloomberg (Aug 2024) quoting operator

notes: Niger section ~1,275 km, Benin section ~675 km; export terminal offshore Sèmè-Kpodji. First cargo May 2024; June 2024 attack and Niger–Benin border dispute suspended flows; exports resumed Aug 2024 and continued through 2025 at full 90 kb/d (Agadem Phase 2). Intermediate points approximate.

name: Agadem–Zinder (SORAZ) crude pipeline
notes: Feeds the 20 kb/d SORAZ refinery at Zinder (Agadem Phase 1).

name: Chad–Cameroon Export Pipeline (Doba–Kribi)
operator: TOTCO (Chad section) / COTCO (Cameroon section; Chad SHT 74.83%, Cameroon 25.17% after 2023 transfers)

source.name: EIB / COTCO / Business in Cameroon (COTCO shareholding)
source.table_or_page: EIB project brief; COTCO share transfer 2023

notes: Komé (Doba) – Bélabo – Yaoundé area – Kribi – offshore FSO Kome Kribi 1 (11 km offshore). ExxonMobil sold Doba/TOTCO stake to Savannah Energy (Dec 2022); Chad nationalised those assets March 2023; Cameroon took 20% of COTCO. Throughput 2024 ~120–140 kb/d (Chad total output), well below design. Route points approximate.

name: Koudalwa (Ronier)–Djermaya crude pipeline

source.name: Société des Hydrocarbures du Tchad (SHT) / CNPC

notes: Bongor basin (Ronier/Mimosa fields) to N'Djamena (Djermaya) refinery. A ~120 km link from Bongor basin to the Komé export system allows CNPC exports via Chad–Cameroon (from 2014).

name: Medgaz (Hassi R'Mel–Beni Saf–Almería)
operator: Medgaz S.A. (Sonatrach 51%, Naturgy 49%); onshore GZ4 by Sonatrach
notes: 547 km onshore (GZ4) + 210 km subsea across the Alboran Sea. Only Algeria–Spain link since GME closure (2021).

name: Transmed / Enrico Mattei Pipeline (Hassi R'Mel–Tunisia–Sicily–Minerbio)
operator: Sonatrach (GG1 Algerian section), SERGAZ/SOTUGAT (Tunisia), TMPC & Snam (Italy)
diametre: 48 in onshore; 2×20 in + 3×26 in subsea (Sicily Channel)

source.name: Snam / Sonatrach; CIDOB analysis of 2024 volumes

notes: Algerian section GG1 (Hassi R'Mel–Oued Saf-Saf, 550 km) + Tunisian section (370 km) + Sicily Channel crossing (155 km) + Italian section. Main Algerian export route to Italy.

name: Maghreb–Europe Gas Pipeline (GME / Pedro Durán Farell)
diametre: 48 in onshore / 2×22 in subsea (Strait of Gibraltar)
capacity: 12 bcm/y (Algeria–Spain flows halted 31 Oct 2021; reverse flow Spain→Morocco ~1 bcm/y since 2022)
notes: Algerian transit through Morocco ended 31 Oct 2021 (contract non-renewal). Pipeline physically intact; used in reverse (Spain→Morocco regasified LNG) to feed Tahaddart and Aïn Beni Mathar power plants. Algeria rejected 2024–2025 EU requests to reopen westbound flows.

name: GZ1/GZ2/GZ3 Hassi R'Mel–Arzew gas trunk lines
capacity: ~45 bcm/y combined (feeds Arzew LNG GL1Z/GL2Z/GL3Z and export/domestic grid)
notes: GZ1 1976, GZ2 1981, GZ3 1990s; capacity combined figure is an industry estimate. Coordinates for Hassi R'Mel and Arzew terminals; intermediate point approximate.

name: GK1/GK2 Hassi R'Mel–Skikda gas trunk lines
capacity: ~20 bcm/y combined (feeds Skikda LNG GL1K and eastern grid)
notes: Often referred to in the brief as 'GR' lines; Sonatrach nomenclature is GK (Hassi R'Mel→Skikda). Capacity estimate.

name: GR1/GR2 Rhourde Nouss–Hassi R'Mel gas trunk lines
notes: Gather south-eastern gas (Rhourde Nouss, Alrar, In Amenas, Tin Fouyé Tabankort, Hassi Messaoud associated gas) into the Hassi R'Mel hub. Capacity estimate.

name: GR5 Reggane/Timimoun–Hassi R'Mel gas trunk line
capacity: ~8 bcm/y (South-West gas: Reggane Nord, Timimoun, Touat)
notes: Evacuates the Reggane/Timimoun/Touat gas projects (2017–2019 start-ups) to Hassi R'Mel.

name: OZ1/OZ2 Haoud El Hamra–Arzew crude pipelines
notes: OZ1 commissioned 1966, OZ2 2005. Haoud El Hamra is the Hassi Messaoud crude hub.

name: OK1 Haoud El Hamra–Skikda crude pipeline
notes: Feeds Skikda refinery and export terminal.

name: OB1 Haoud El Hamra–Béjaïa crude pipeline
notes: Algeria's first crude export line (1959).

name: OT1 In Amenas–La Skhirra crude pipeline (TRAPSA)
notes: Cross-border crude line to the Tunisian terminal of La Skhirra (Gulf of Gabès).

name: Hassi R'Mel gas hub collector & LPG/condensate lines (LZ1, NK1)
diametre: various (LZ1 24 in LPG Hassi R'Mel–Arzew; NK1 condensate Hassi Messaoud–Skikda)
notes: Composite record for the Hassi R'Mel hub product lines; LZ1 (LPG, 1984) shown; NK1 condensate line Hassi Messaoud–Skikda not drawn. Split if the platform needs one record per line.

name: Greenstream (Mellitah–Gela)

source.name: Eni / GEM
source.table_or_page: Western Libya Gas Project; GEM 'Greenstream Pipeline'

notes: Fed by Wafa (onshore) and Bahr Essalam (offshore) via Mellitah complex; Structures A&E (FID 2023, first gas 2026) to backfill declining supply.

name: Sarir–Tobruk (Marsa El Hariga) crude pipeline

source.name: NOC Libya / GEM
source.table_or_page: AGOCO Sarir operations; GEM Libya pipelines category

notes: Also carries Messla crude. Terminal Marsa El Hariga (Tobruk).

name: Waha (Gialo/Dahra/Samah)–Es Sider crude pipelines
operator: Waha Oil Company (NOC 59%, ConocoPhillips 16.33%, TotalEnergies 16.33%, Eni 8.33%)
notes: Es Sider is Libya's largest export terminal; Waha expansion (North Gialo, NC-98) in progress 2024–2025. Route approximate.

name: El Sharara–Zawiya crude pipeline
operator: Akakus Oil Operations (NOC, Repsol, OMV, TotalEnergies, Equinor)
notes: 340 km Sharara–Hamada + 383 km Hamada–Zawiya refinery/terminal. Repeated force majeure events (2024 blockade Jan–Feb; Aug–Oct 2024) then record 306 kb/d at Sharara in 2025.

name: El Feel–El Sharara crude link
notes: El Feel (Elephant) crude routed via Sharara to Zawiya (and Mellitah).

name: Wafa–Mellitah oil & gas pipelines (Western Libya Gas Project)
notes: Parallel gas and condensate/oil lines from the Wafa field (Ghadames basin, Algerian border) to the Mellitah complex; Greenstream feed.

name: Bahr Essalam / Bouri offshore lines to Mellitah
notes: Sabratha platform → Mellitah gas plant. Bouri oil is exported via the Sloug FSO; Structures A&E will tie into this system.

name: SUMED (Suez–Mediterranean) crude pipeline
operator: Arab Petroleum Pipelines Co. (EGPC 50%, Saudi Aramco 15%, ADNOC 15%, KPC 15%, QP 5%)
notes: Ain Sukhna (Gulf of Suez) to Sidi Kerir (Alexandria). Volumes fell 2024 with Red Sea rerouting, then rebounded strongly in 2026.

name: Arab Gas Pipeline (AGP) – Arish–Taba–Aqaba–Rehab–Jaber
notes: Egypt→Jordan flows resumed at low volumes; Jordanian section also carries Israeli (Leviathan) gas southward to Egypt since 2020 (reverse use). Syria/Lebanon extensions largely idle. Oct 2024 Egypt–Jordan agreement for Quweira/Aqaba industrial supply.

name: EMG / El Arish–Ashkelon pipeline (reverse flow Israel→Egypt)
operator: East Mediterranean Gas (EMG; Chevron/Delek/EGAS consortium since 2019)
capacity: ~7 bcm/y (Israel→Egypt ~1.0–1.2 bcf/d in 2024–2025; Ashdod–Ashkelon link 2025 adds ~2 bcm/y)
notes: Built for Egypt→Israel exports (2008–2012), reversed 2020 to carry Israeli Leviathan/Tamar gas to Egypt (feeding Idku/Damietta LNG and domestic demand). Flows interrupted during Israeli field shut-ins (Oct 2023, June 2025).

name: GASCO National Gas Grid – Nile Delta trunk (Damietta–Cairo–Alexandria)
notes: Composite record: total high-pressure grid ~7,500 km; coordinates trace the Damietta–Cairo–Alexandria backbone only. Split by trunk line if needed.

name: Western Desert Gas Pipeline (Obaiyed/Abu Gharadig–Amreya)
notes: Carries Khalda/Obaiyed/Abu Gharadig gas to the Western Desert Gas Complex and Alexandria; geometry approximate.

name: Zohr subsea export trunklines (Zohr–Port Said onshore plant)
notes: Field ~190 km north of Port Said; field coordinate approximate.

name: Cabinda onshore/offshore gathering to Malongo terminal (Block 0)
operator: Cabinda Gulf Oil Company (Chevron 39.2%, Sonangol 41%, TotalEnergies 10%, Eni 9.8%)
notes: Composite record for the Block 0 (Areas A/B) trunklines from Takula, Malongo, Nemba, Sanha complexes to the Malongo terminal. No single public pipeline dataset; geometry indicative only.

name: Congo River Crossing Pipeline (Cabinda–Soyo gas)
notes: Carries Block 0/14 associated gas across the Congo River mouth to the Angola LNG plant at Soyo. Sanha Lean Gas Connection (2023) added non-associated gas.

name: Angola LNG offshore gas gathering system (Blocks 15/17/18 → Soyo)
notes: Composite record of the subsea trunklines from deepwater blocks to Soyo; New Gas Consortium (Quiluma & Maboqueiro, first gas 2026) will add a dedicated line.

name: Lobito–Lusaka products pipeline

source.name: Sonangol / Wikipedia summary of 2024 technical study

notes: Tied to the planned 200 kb/d Lobito refinery (financing gap ~USD 4.8 bn, 2025). Concept-level; secondary source.

name: Lobito refinery crude supply line
notes: Refinery at pre-construction/financing stage; crude to be delivered by tanker to a new marine terminal with short onshore lines. Placeholder record.

name: Moho-Bilondo / Nkossa offshore export lines to Djeno terminal
notes: Composite record: Moho Nord (Likouf FPU/TLP) and Nkossa/Yanga-Sendji fields export via subsea lines to Djeno; geometry indicative.

name: Marine XII gas pipeline (Litchendjili/Nené → Djeno gas plant → CEC power plant)
operator: Eni Congo (Marine XII: Eni 65%, Lukoil 25%, SNPC 10%)
capacity: ~120 mmcf/d to Centrale Électrique du Congo
notes: Since 2024 Marine XII gas also feeds Tango FLNG and (Dec 2025) Nguya FLNG offshore via new subsea lines.

name: Rabi–Cap Lopez crude pipeline
operator: Gabon Oil Company (ex-Assala Energy, ex-Shell Gabon; state acquisition 2024)
notes: Rabi-Kounga to Cap Lopez export terminal (Port-Gentil). Also carries Toucan/Koula/Gamba-Ivinga pipelines connections. Intermediate point approximate.

name: Gamba–Ivinga to Gamba terminal
notes: Gabon's original 1960s export terminal; geometry indicative.

name: Atuabo–Aboadze (Takoradi) gas pipeline (Western Corridor)
notes: Jubilee gas landed at Atuabo GPP (2014/15); Sinopec EPC. Tie-in to WAGP at Takoradi (2019) enables eastward flow to Tema.

name: Takoradi–Tema Interconnection (TTIP, WAGP reverse flow)
notes: Uses WAGP's Takoradi–Tema segment in reverse; not a new pipe. Recorded separately for network-topology purposes.

name: Jubilee gas export pipeline (FPSO Kwame Nkrumah → Atuabo)
notes: Gas processed at Atuabo GPP.

name: Sankofa–Gye Nyame (OCTP) gas pipeline to Sanzule ORF
notes: Onshore Receiving Facility at Sanzule links to the Ghana Gas Western Corridor.

name: CI-27 Foxtrot/Marlin/Manta gas pipelines to Abidjan (Vridi)
notes: Supplies ~75% of Ivorian gas to Vridi/Azito/CIPREL power plants. Geometry indicative (search verification unavailable this session).

name: Baleine gas export pipeline (FPSO Baleine → Abidjan)
operator: Eni Côte d'Ivoire (Baleine: Eni 53%→ after Vitol entry 2025 Eni/Vitol/Petroci)
notes: 100% of Baleine gas supplies domestic power via the Phase 1 pipeline. Length/route approximate.

name: Greater Tortue Ahmeyim (GTA) subsea gas export system

source.name: bp / Kosmos Energy
source.table_or_page: First cargo 17 Apr 2025; first gas 2 Jan 2025

notes: Wells at ~2,850 m water depth ~120 km offshore → FPSO 40 km offshore → FLNG Gimi at the nearshore hub 10 km offshore on the Senegal–Mauritania maritime border. Coordinates approximate along the 16.07°N border line.

name: Réseau Gazier du Sénégal (RGS) – Saint-Louis–Dakar–Mbour gas-to-power network
notes: Domestic network to bring GTA/Yakaar-Teranga gas to power plants (Cap des Biches, Saint-Louis). Feasibility stage.

name: Bipaga–Mpolongwe (Kribi) gas pipeline
notes: Sanaga Sud gas processed at Bipaga (Perenco) then piped by SNH to KPDC's Kribi power plant. Perenco's Bipaga processing centre expansion started production July 2024.

name: Sanaga Sud offshore gas pipeline to Bipaga
notes: Also feeds the Hilli Episeyo FLNG (2018) offshore Kribi via a separate riser. Geometry indicative.

name: Logbaba–Douala gas distribution network
notes: Onshore Douala basin gas to industrial customers in Douala.

name: Rio del Rey offshore lines to Kole terminal
notes: Composite record of gathering lines to the Kole FSO/terminal; geometry indicative.

name: ROMPCO (Temane–Secunda)
operator: ROMPCO (Sasol 30%, CEF 30%, iGas → Reatile 30%? see note)
notes: Only gas import route into South Africa; Pande/Temane depletion expected from ~2027 ('gas cliff'). Shareholding: Sasol 30%, CEF 30%, Reatile (acquired iGas/... ) — verify. Route points approximate.

name: Lilly pipeline (Secunda–Richards Bay)
notes: Delivers Secunda synthetic/natural gas to KwaZulu-Natal (Newcastle, Richards Bay). Length/diameter from public Sasol network descriptions; unverified this session.

name: Transnet New Multi-Product Pipeline (NMPP) Durban–Jameson Park
capacity: ~4.4 bn litres/y initial (design up to ~8.7 bn litres/y)
notes: Replaces the 1965 12-in Durban–Johannesburg Pipeline (DJP); full multi-product operation from 2017/18. Capacity figures unverified this session.

name: F-A platform–Mossel Bay gas pipeline (PetroSA)
notes: Feedstock for the Mossel Bay GTL refinery; offshore gas (F-A, E-M, South Coast) depleted and GTL plant idle since 2020. Restart options (LNG import / Block 11B/12B) unresolved.

name: Kudu gas pipeline (Kudu field → Uubvlei/Oranjemund power plant)
notes: Kudu (1.3 tcf, discovered 1974) development repeatedly deferred; BW Energy studying a smaller FPSO-based gas-to-power option. Status: concept as of 2025.

name: Matadi (Ango-Ango)–Kinshasa products pipeline (SEP Congo)
operator: SEP Congo (Services des Entreprises Pétrolières Congolaises)

source.name: SEP Congo / GEM
source.table_or_page: SEP Congo pipeline page; GEM 'Matadi-Kinshasa Pipeline'

notes: SEP Congo reports a total pipeline network of 720 km (Matadi–Kinshasa trunk plus branches to N'Djili airport, Masina, Kinshasa-Ville); trunk length ~365 km. Three pumping stations. Capacity/diameter indicative.

name: Alen–Punta Europa gas pipeline

source.name: Chevron / Ministry of Mines & Hydrocarbons GNQ (via NS Energy summary)

notes: Backfills the Alba LPG plant and EG LNG at Punta Europa (Bioko). Foundation of the 'Gas Mega Hub' with Aseng/Alba tie-ins.

name: Alba field–Punta Europa gas & condensate lines
notes: Alba is in decline; Alen backfill (2021) and Aseng gas tie-in sustain Punta Europa.

name: Gulf of Guinea Gas Pipeline (Nigeria–Equatorial Guinea)
operator: NNPC / Ministry of Mines & Hydrocarbons GNQ

source.name: Ministry of Mines & Hydrocarbons GNQ (statement via Energy Chamber)

notes: MoU-level; would route Nigerian gas to Punta Europa LNG. No FEED published.
